chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali from his father from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about an animal slaughtered facing away from the Qibla, so he said, 'Eat it; there is no harm with that unless it was done deliberately.' I asked him about a man who slaughtered but did not mention the Name, so he said, 'If he was forgetful, let him mention the Name when he remembers and say, 'In the Name of Allah,' over its beginning and over its end.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on meat slaughtered facing away from the Qibla or if the slaughterer forgot to say Bismillah?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the distinction between minor defects in slaughter orientation and the essential requirement of invoking Allah's name. He establishes that facing away from the Qibla does not invalidate the meat unless done deliberately, while for those who forgot the invocation, a simple recitation upon remembering suffices, reflecting the Shia principle of ease in ritual purity and consumption.
